findings.title: Overly technical language obscures what is shared with the service
findings.evidence: “Leverage our multimodal generative narrative engine to synthesise bespoke, heirloom-grade story artefacts from your household's lived-experience corpus.”
findings.why: I am being asked to think about my child's data, and corporate jargon does not tell me what information is collected, retained, shared, or used to train AI.

findings.title: Main illustration has no accessible description
findings.evidence: [image (no description) 430x440]
findings.why: The image gives no information to anyone using a screen reader and appears unexplained to me visually as well.

findings.title: Creation action does not disclose the next step
findings.evidence: [5] link “Proceed →”
findings.why: I cannot tell whether I will be logging in, uploading photographs, or immediately sharing child data.

findings.title: Printed price is not visible on the landing page
findings.evidence: “Free digital preview · Printed hardcovers shipped across the UK”
findings.why: I need to know whether this is a genuinely free service or an expensive printed product before investing time and sharing personal information.

findings.title: Email and password fields lack persistent visible labels
findings.evidence: Items [5] and [6] are described as textboxes with no label and rely on the placeholders “Email” and “Password”.
findings.why: Placeholders are less accessible and can be forgotten once typing begins, especially for people using assistive technology or returning to the form.

findings.title: Unexplained technical profile-sync error
findings.evidence: “Error 0x80070057: profile sync incomplete.”
findings.why: I cannot tell whether this concerns login data, family information, or some other profile field. An unexplained failure makes me fear that something may be lost or recorded incorrectly.

findings.title: Technical error shown without status or effect
findings.evidence: The warning only says “profile sync incomplete” and does not state whether the rest of the account works.
findings.why: I do not know whether it is safe to create a book or whether my details will be incomplete.

findings.title: Footer links have very low contrast
findings.evidence: The visible “Privacy,” “Terms,” and “Contact” links are extremely pale against the footer background.
findings.why: The privacy link is important to me, and I had to focus on the faint footer to notice it.

findings.title: Technical error remains unexplained
findings.evidence: “Error 0x80070057: profile sync incomplete.”
findings.why: An unexplained error about profile syncing makes me question whether my account and family information will be saved reliably.

findings.title: Data retention and deletion are unspecified
findings.evidence: “Uploaded images may be retained to improve our services”
findings.why: I need to know how long Nikolai’s photo and story will be kept and whether I can delete them.

findings.title: Technology partners are unidentified
findings.evidence: “may be processed by our technology partners”
findings.why: I cannot assess who can see my child’s photograph or whether it is used for AI training without knowing the recipients.

findings.title: Purpose of image processing is too vague
findings.evidence: “to create your book” and “improve our services”
findings.why: Creating my book is understandable, but “improve our services” is broad enough that I do not know what secondary use is occurring.

findings.title: Terms are not a substitute for full terms
findings.evidence: “Digital previews are provided as-is.”
findings.why: I need to know what happens if a generated book contains errors or does not meet the agreed description, and I need clear terms before ordering.

findings.title: Cancellation and refund limitation is abrupt
findings.evidence: “Printed orders are non-refundable once production begins.”
findings.why: This is a significant restriction and I cannot judge the real cost and risk without knowing the production start point, cancellation rules and what happens if the book is damaged or incorrect.

findings.title: Relationship is preselected without a choice
findings.evidence: [11] displays “Grandparent” as the selected option before I make a selection.
findings.why: A preselected answer can silently put inaccurate information about my family into a personalised story, and it recalls the sort of default choices I distrust.

findings.title: No reminder of data-use limits before personal details
findings.evidence: The form immediately requests a child's name, age, pronouns and appearance, while the only policy information is in the footer links “Privacy” and “Terms”.
findings.why: Before entering details about Nikolai, I want a concise reminder of how this information will be used, whether it is used to train AI, and how it can be deleted.

findings.title: Mother is not named as a relationship option
findings.evidence: [11] offers “Grandparent | Parent | Sibling | Friend | Pet | Other” rather than a specific “Mother” option.
findings.why: Mama is a character in our memory, and “Parent” is technically correct but less natural and precise than “Mother.”

findings.title: Fields are not marked optional
findings.evidence: [16] “Where does the story happen?”, [17] “A special object”, and [18] “Tell us the memory or idea behind your story” have no “optional” label.
findings.why: It is unclear whether all three fields are compulsory, particularly because the previous appearance field was explicitly marked “(optional)”. I cannot tell whether one small omission will prevent me from continuing.

findings.title: Reading-level labels require specialist knowledge
findings.evidence: “Reading level” followed by “Lexile BR–200L” and “Lexile 200L–500L”
findings.why: I want to choose a genuinely appropriate level for a six-year-old, but the site does not explain what BR–200L or 200L–500L means in practical terms.

findings.title: Preselected options are not explained
findings.evidence: [22] “Lexile 200L–500L” (checked) and [25] “Watercolour — soft and dreamy” (checked)
findings.why: I can accept the choices, but I cannot tell whether they were intelligently recommended or simply the site defaults.

findings.title: Photo upload lacks specific privacy disclosure
findings.evidence: “Upload a clear photo of your child's face so the illustrations look like them.” The page itself does not explain whether the image is used for AI training, who can access it, how long it is retained, or how it can be deleted.
findings.why: A child's photograph is sensitive personal information, and I will not upload it without knowing these consequences.

findings.title: File control has no explicit accessible label
findings.evidence: [30] file-upload (no label), with only the native text “Choose file”
findings.why: A visible field label and accessible control name would make it clear what kind of file is being selected and why.

findings.title: Footer text has weak contrast
findings.evidence: The “Privacy,” “Terms,” and “Contact” links and “© 2026 StoryHearth Ltd.” appear extremely faint against the background.
findings.why: Important legal and contact links are difficult to see, particularly when I am specifically checking privacy terms.

findings.title: Selected illustration style was not applied
findings.evidence: The page says “Illustration style: Pop-art comic,” while the earlier selection was “Watercolour — soft and dreamy.”
findings.why: I chose the style specifically to make the book feel gentle and suitable for a six-year-old. An unexpected style suggests the result may not reflect my choices.

findings.title: Typographical error in the book title
findings.evidence: The cover and heading read “The Magical Adventrue of Nikolai.”
findings.why: It makes the personalised book look unfinished and less trustworthy, especially when this may be printed.

findings.title: The cover does not clearly show the requested school-gate memory
findings.evidence: The cover shows a simple house-like building, Nikolai, a sun, and a grey stone, but not a clear school gate or rainy setting.
findings.why: The memory was about Nikolai’s first morning at a new school on a rainy morning. The cover does not yet make that personal connection obvious.

findings.title: Paid regeneration option is prominent before I have inspected the book
findings.evidence: [8] “Regenerate entire book – $4.99” appears below the preview.
findings.why: I want to assess the book and its pricing before spending anything, and the regeneration price needs to be clearly explained.

findings.title: Generated cover does not reflect the supplied character details
findings.evidence: I entered “blond straight hair, gap in his front teeth, yellow raincoat,” but the cover shows Nikolai with blond hair, no visible gap in his front teeth, and no yellow raincoat.
findings.why: This is Nikolai's personal story, and the cover should not look as though the details I carefully supplied were ignored.

findings.title: The final sentence is incomplete
findings.evidence: “And from that day on, whenever Nikolai looked up at the sky, he would always remember”
findings.why: It leaves the most important final thought unfinished, making the book feel careless rather than comforting or reassuring.

findings.title: The ending introduces an unrelated idea
findings.evidence: “whenever Nikolai looked up at the sky”
findings.why: The supplied memory concerns a rainy school gate and a stone from Varna, not the sky, so the ending does not feel personal.

findings.title: Optional gift wrap is pre-selected
findings.evidence: [6] checkbox "Premium gift wrap" (checked), with "£7.99" added and "Total £45.97"
findings.why: I am not comfortable being charged for something I did not choose, and it makes the advertised checkout total misleading.

findings.title: Countdown timer creates purchase pressure
findings.evidence: "Your price is reserved for 09:57"
findings.why: I distrust artificial urgency, especially before I have even inspected the finished book or final terms.

findings.title: Base delivery-inclusive price is not made prominent
findings.evidence: "Hardcover £24.99", "Shipping & handling £12.99", and "Total £45.97"
findings.why: I need to distinguish the product price, unavoidable delivery charge and optional extras without doing my own arithmetic.

findings.title: Poorly generated book title is carried into the order
findings.evidence: "Hardcover: The Magical Adventrue of Nikolai"
findings.why: The misspelling makes the product look unfinished and would be embarrassing in a physical book.

findings.title: emotional_resonance

findings.title: language

findings.title: coherence
findings.evidence: The book begins at a rainy school morning, but the story abruptly changes to "One evening" with no transition.

findings.title: text_image_fit

findings.title: emotional_resonance

findings.title: text_image_fit
findings.evidence: The text mentions a lantern and winding path, but neither is clearly depicted; the picture instead retains the house.

findings.title: language
findings.evidence: "Uncle Bartholomew" appears as an unexplained heading immediately before the dialogue.

findings.title: fidelity
findings.evidence: The new school and Mama disappear and are replaced by a deep forest, a red balloon and a threat that Nikolai will never be found.

findings.title: coherence
findings.evidence: There is no transition from the school approach to "Deep in the woods," and the threat is never addressed.

findings.title: age_fit
findings.evidence: "the shadows grew teeth" and the claim that nobody would ever find him introduce frightening imagery and a serious danger for the target age.

findings.title: text_image_fit
findings.evidence: I7 has a few trees and darkness but does not show the stated toothed shadows, whispering threat or clutching action.

findings.title: fidelity
findings.evidence: The shiny red balloon is invented and is not the special object supplied for the story.

findings.title: coherence
findings.evidence: "Once upon a time" restarts the story, and "At last the sun came out" resolves a conflict that has not been shown.

findings.title: fidelity
findings.evidence: Nikolai is no longer described as scared, and the brave stone and Mama are absent from the resolution.

findings.title: text_image_fit
findings.evidence: The text says he skipped home happier than ever, but I8 shows him standing still beside a house, with no visible happiness or movement.

findings.title: character_consistency
findings.evidence: Nikolai is again in a green top without the requested yellow raincoat, despite the text referring to rain.

findings.title: language
findings.evidence: The sentence ends at "he would always remember" without an object or punctuation, and "The End" is repeated.

findings.title: coherence
findings.evidence: The final reflection is incomplete and disconnected from the preceding instant happiness.

findings.title: text_image_fit

findings.title: visual_quality

findings.title: safety concern
findings.evidence: The threatening forest passage—"the shadows grew teeth" and "no one would ever find Nikolai again"—may intensify anxiety in a six-year-old, especially given the stated reason for the book.

findings.title: safety concern
findings.evidence: The book contains no graphic violence or sexual content, and no payment information or sensitive child data is visibly exposed in the captures.

findings.title: safety concern
findings.evidence: The privacy, AI-training, retention, deletion and cancellation terms cannot be judged from the footer labels alone; their absence from the checkout view is a trust concern rather than evidence of harmful data use.
